translations.literal: Zhao first with a great host prepared at Liyang; seeing Chui go to the western ford, he abandoned camp and went west to block.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had massed at Liyang; seeing Chui move west, he marched west to block him.

sentences.zh: 垂潛遣其桂林王慕容鎮、驃騎慕容國于黎陽津夜濟，壁于河南。

translations.literal: Chui secretly sent his Prince of Guilin Murong Zhen and the Agile Cavalry Murong Guo to cross at the Liyang ford by night and wall on the south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Chui secretly sent Murong Zhen and Murong Guo to cross by night and fortify south of the river.

sentences.zh: 釗聞而奔還，士眾疲渴，走歸滑台，釗攜妻子率數百騎北趣白鹿山。

translations.literal: Zhao heard and ran back; the soldiers were weary and thirsty, fled back to Huatai; Zhao took wife and children and led several hundred horsemen north toward Bailu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao turned back; his men, spent and thirsty, fled to Huatai; Zhao took his family and a few hundred horse and ran for Bailu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 農追擊，盡擒其眾，釗單騎奔長子。

translations.literal: Nong pursued, captured all his host; Zhao alone on a single horse fled to Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: Nong pursued and took them all; Zhao alone escaped to Changzi.

sentences.zh: 釗所統七郡戶三萬八千皆安堵如故。

translations.literal: The seven commanderies under Zhao's rule, thirty-eight thousand households, were all settled as before.
translations.idiomatic: The seven commanderies, thirty-eight thousand households, were left undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 徙徐州流人七千餘戶于黎陽。

translations.literal: He moved seven thousand more households of refugees from Xuzhou to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled seven thousand refugees from Xuzhou at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 於是議征長子。

translations.literal: Thereupon they deliberated attacking Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: Then they debated an attack on Changzi.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸諫，以慕容永未有釁，連歲征役，士卒疲怠，請俟他年。

translations.literal: The generals all remonstrated that Murong Yong had not yet given offense, and year after year campaigns had wearied the soldiers— they asked to wait for another year.
translations.idiomatic: His officers objected that Murong Yong had given no cause, that years of war had exhausted the troops, and begged to wait.

sentences.zh: 垂將從之，及聞慕容德之策，笑曰：「吾計決矣。

translations.literal: Chui was about to follow this; when he heard Murong De's plan he smiled and said, "My decision is made.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to agree; then he heard Murong De's counsel and said, "My mind is made up.

sentences.zh: 且吾投老，扣囊底智，足以克之，不復留逆賊以累子孫也。

translations.literal: Moreover I am old; tapping the bottom of the bag's wisdom is enough to overcome him—I will not leave this rebel to burden my sons and grandsons."
translations.idiomatic: I am old, but what wisdom remains in the bottom of the bag is enough to crush him—I will not leave this rebel to my heirs."

sentences.zh: 」乃發步騎七萬，遣其丹陽王慕容贊、龍驤張崇攻永弟支于晉陽。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sent seventy thousand foot and horse, dispatched his Prince of Danyang Murong Zan and the Dragon-soaring Zhang Chong to attack Yong's younger brother Zhi at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent seventy thousand men, and Murong Zan and Zhang Chong against Yong's brother Zhi at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 永遣其將刁雲、慕容鐘率眾五萬屯潞川。

translations.literal: Yong sent his generals Diao Yun and Murong Zhong with fifty thousand to encamp at Luchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent Diao Yun and Murong Zhong with fifty thousand to hold Luchuan.

sentences.zh: 垂遣慕容楷出自滏口，慕容農入自壺關，垂頓於鄴之西南，月餘不進。

translations.literal: Chui sent Murong Kai out from Fukou, Murong Nong in from Huguan, Chui himself halted southwest of Ye for more than a month without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Chui sent Kai through Fukou and Nong through Huguan, and himself camped southwest of Ye for a month without moving.

sentences.zh: 永謂垂詭道伐之，乃攝諸軍還杜太行軹關。

translations.literal: Yong thought Chui was using a deceptive route to attack him and therefore gathered all his armies back to guard the Zhatai Pass at Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Yong thought it a feint and pulled all his men back to guard Zhatai Pass.

sentences.zh: 垂進師入自天井關，至於壺壁。

translations.literal: Chui advanced the army entering from Tianjing Pass, reaching Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Chui entered by Tianjing Pass and reached Hubei.

sentences.zh: 永率精卒五萬來距，阻河曲以自固，馳使請戰。

translations.literal: Yong led elite troops fifty thousand to block; he blocked the river bend to hold firm, sent a swift messenger to request battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yong came with fifty thousand picked men, blocked the river bend, and challenged him to fight.

sentences.zh: 垂列陣於壺避之南，農、楷分為二翼，慕容國伏千兵於深澗，與永大戰。

translations.literal: Chui arrayed south of Hubi; Nong and Kai divided into two wings; Murong Guo hid a thousand troops in a deep ravine and fought a great battle with Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Chui formed south of Hubi; Nong and Kai took the wings; Guo hid a thousand men in a ravine; the great battle was joined.

sentences.zh: 垂引軍偽退，永追奔數里，國發伏兵馳斷其後，楷、農夾擊之，永師大敗，斬首八千餘級，永奔還長子。

translations.literal: Chui led the army in feigned retreat; Yong pursued several li; Guo sent the ambush troops at the gallop to cut his rear; Kai and Nong struck from both sides; Yong's army was greatly defeated, severed heads more than eight thousand; Yong fled back to Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: Chui feigned retreat; Yong pursued; Guo struck his rear; Kai and Nong closed on the flanks; eight thousand fell; Yong fled to Changzi.

sentences.zh: 慕容贊攻克晉陽。

translations.literal: Murong Zan took Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zan took Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 垂進圍長子，永將賈韜潛為內應。

translations.literal: Chui advanced to besiege Changzi; Yong's general Jia Tao secretly acted as inner responder.
translations.idiomatic: Chui besieged Changzi; Yong's officer Jia Tao plotted treason within.

sentences.zh: 垂進軍入城，永奔北門，為前驅所獲，於是數而戮之，並其所署公卿刁雲等三十餘人。

translations.literal: Chui advanced the army into the city; Yong fled to the north gate and was seized by the vanguard; thereupon he enumerated his crimes and executed him, together with the dukes and ministers he had appointed, Diao Yun and more than thirty others.
translations.idiomatic: Chui entered the city; Yong was taken at the north gate, judged, and executed with Diao Yun and more than thirty of his officers.

sentences.zh: 永所統新舊八郡戶七萬六千八百及乘輿、服御、伎樂、珍寶悉獲之，於是品物具矣。

translations.literal: The eight commanderies old and new under Yong, seventy-six thousand eight hundred households, and chariots, robes, musicians, and treasures were all obtained; at once the categories of things were complete.
translations.idiomatic: He took eight commanderies, seventy-six thousand eight hundred households, and Yong's chariots, robes, musicians, and treasure—the regalia was complete.

sentences.zh: 使慕容農略地河南，攻廩丘、陽城，皆克之，太山、琅邪諸郡皆委城奔潰，農進師臨海，置守宰而還。

translations.literal: He sent Murong Nong to seize lands in Henan, attack Lianqiu and Yangcheng—all were taken; Taishan, Langye, and the various commanderies all abandoned their cities and fled in collapse; Nong advanced the army to the sea, set guards and magistrates, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Nong swept Henan, took Lianqiu and Yangcheng, and the commanderies of Taishan and Langye fell away; he reached the sea, set magistrates, and returned.

sentences.zh: 垂告捷于龍城之廟。

translations.literal: Chui reported victory at the temple in Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chui reported victory at the Longcheng temple.

sentences.zh: 遣其太子寶及農與慕容麟等率眾八萬伐魏，慕容德、慕容紹以步騎一萬八千為寶後繼。

translations.literal: He sent his Heir Bao and Nong with Murong Lin and others to lead eighty thousand to attack Wei; Murong De and Murong Shao with eighteen thousand foot and horse followed as Bao's rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Bao and Nong with eighty thousand against Wei; De and Shao followed with eighteen thousand.

sentences.zh: 魏聞寶將至，徙往河西。

translations.literal: Wei, hearing Bao was about to arrive, moved west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei fled west of the river when they heard Bao was coming.

sentences.zh: 寶進師臨河，懼不敢濟。

translations.literal: Bao advanced the army to the river and, in fear, did not dare cross.
translations.idiomatic: Bao reached the river and dared not cross.

sentences.zh: 還次參合，忽有大風黑氣，狀若堤防，或高或下，臨覆軍上。

translations.literal: Returning to camp at Canhe, suddenly there was a great wind and black vapor, shaped like a dike, now high now low, hanging over and covering the army.
translations.idiomatic: Marching back to Canhe, a black storm like a wall rose over the army.

sentences.zh: 沙門支曇猛言於寶曰：「風氣暴迅，魏軍將至之候，宜遣兵禦之。

translations.literal: The monk Zhi Tanmeng said to Bao, "The wind and vapor are violently swift—a sign the Wei army is about to arrive; you should send troops to guard against the unforeseen."
translations.idiomatic: The monk Zhi Tanmeng told Bao, "This wind means the Wei are coming—you must post guards."

sentences.zh: 」寶笑而不納。

translations.literal: " Bao smiled and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " Bao laughed and would not listen.

sentences.zh: 曇猛固以為言，乃遣麟率騎三萬為後殿，以禦非常。

translations.literal: Tanmeng firmly spoke again; thereupon he sent Lin with thirty thousand horsemen as the rear guard to guard against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: Tanmeng pressed him again; Bao sent Lin with thirty thousand horse as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 麟以曇猛言為虛，縱騎遊獵。

translations.literal: Lin took Tanmeng's words as empty and let the horsemen roam in the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Lin thought the monk spoke folly and let his men hunt.

sentences.zh: 俄而黃霧四塞，日月晦冥，是夜魏師大至，三軍奔潰，寶與德等數千騎奔免，士眾還者十一二，紹死之。

translations.literal: Soon yellow mist filled the four quarters, sun and moon were dark; that night the Wei army arrived in force; the three armies fled in collapse; Bao with De and others, several thousand horsemen, escaped; of the soldiers who returned, one or two in ten; Shao died.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow fog swallowed the field; that night the Wei came in force; the army broke; Bao and De escaped with a few thousand horse; nine in ten were lost; Shao was killed.

sentences.zh: 初，寶至幽州，所乘車軸無故自折。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Bao reached Youzhou, the axle of the carriage he rode broke for no reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao came to Youzhou, the axle of his carriage had snapped without cause.

sentences.zh: 術士靳安以為大凶，固勸寶還，寶怒不從，故及於敗。

translations.literal: The diviner Jin An took this as a great ill omen and firmly urged Bao to return; Bao in anger did not follow, and therefore met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The diviner Jin An called it deadly ill luck and begged him to turn back; Bao in anger refused, and so met ruin.

sentences.zh: 寶恨參合之敗，屢言魏有可乘之機。

translations.literal: Bao hated the defeat at Canhe and repeatedly said Wei had a chance to be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Bao brooded on Canhe and kept saying Wei could be struck.

sentences.zh: 慕容德亦曰：「魏人狃於參合之役，有陵太子之心，宜及聖略，摧其銳志。

translations.literal: Murong De also said, "The Wei men, accustomed to the battle at Canhe, have the mind to look down on the Heir—while the sacred strategy is fresh, crush their sharp will."
translations.idiomatic: Murong De said, "The Wei, bloated by Canhe, despise the heir—strike now while your father's power is whole."

sentences.zh: 」垂從之，留德守中山，自率大眾出參合，鑿山開道，次於獵嶺。

translations.literal: " Chui followed this, left De to guard Zhongshan, himself led the great host out of Canhe, cut through the mountains and opened a road, and halted at Lie Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: " Chui agreed, left De at Zhongshan, marched from Canhe, cut a road through the mountains, and camped at Lie Ridge.

sentences.zh: 遣寶與農出天門，征北慕容隆、征西慕容盛逾青山，襲魏陳留公泥于平城，陷之，收其眾三萬餘人而還。

translations.literal: He sent Bao and Nong out by Tianmen, the northern expedition Murong Long and the western expedition Murong Sheng crossing Qing Mountain to strike the Wei Chenliu Duke Ni at Pingcheng, took it, and gathered his host of more than thirty thousand and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Bao and Nong by Tianmen, Long and Sheng over Qing Mountain against Ni at Pingcheng; they took it and returned with thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 垂至參合，見往年戰處積骸如山，設弔祭之禮，死者父兄一時號哭，軍中皆慟。

translations.literal: Chui reached Canhe, saw the heaped bones of former years' battle like a mountain, set out rites of mourning and sacrifice; the fathers and elder brothers of the dead all wailed at once, and throughout the army there was grief.
translations.idiomatic: At Canhe he saw the bones of the dead heaped like a hill; he mourned them, and fathers and brothers wailed until the whole army wept.

sentences.zh: 垂慚憤歐血，因而寢疾，乘馬輿而進。

translations.literal: Chui, ashamed and indignant, spat blood; because of this he took to his bed ill, riding in a litter he advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Chui, shamed and raging, coughed blood, fell ill, and was carried forward in a litter.

sentences.zh: 過平城北三十里，疾篤，築燕昌城而還。

translations.literal: Passing thirty li north of Pingcheng, his illness was severe; he built Yanchang city and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li north of Pingcheng his sickness grew grave; he built Yanchang city and turned back.

sentences.zh: 寶等至雲中，聞垂疾，皆引歸。

translations.literal: Bao and the others reached Yunzhong, heard Chui was ill, and all turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Bao and the rest, reaching Yunzhong, heard Chui was dying and turned back.

sentences.zh: 及垂至於平城，或有叛者奔告魏曰：「垂病已亡，輿屍在軍。

translations.literal: When Chui reached Pingcheng, some rebels fled to report to Wei, "Chui is already dead; his corpse is in the army."
translations.idiomatic: At Pingcheng deserters told the Wei, "Chui is dead; his body is with the army."

sentences.zh: 」魏又聞參合大哭，以為信然，乃進兵追之，知平城已陷而退，還館陰山。

translations.literal: " Wei also heard the great wailing at Canhe and took it as true; thereupon they advanced troops in pursuit; learning Pingcheng had fallen they withdrew and returned to lodge at Yin Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: " The Wei heard the mourning at Canhe and believed it; they pursued until they learned Pingcheng had fallen, then withdrew to Yin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 垂至上谷之沮陽，乙太元二十一年死，時年七十一，凡在位十三年。

translations.literal: Chui reached Zuyang in Shanggu; in the twenty-first year of the Taiyuan era he died, aged seventy-one; altogether he held position thirteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Chui reached Zuyang in Shanggu and died in the twenty-first year of Taiyuan, aged seventy-one, having ruled thirteen years.

sentences.zh: 遺令曰：「方今禍難尚殷，喪禮一從簡易，朝終夕殯，事訖成服，三日之後，釋服從政。

translations.literal: His final command said, "Today calamity and hardship are still abundant; mourning rites should all follow simplicity—morning ended, evening encoffined, affairs finished then don the hemp garment; after three days, remove the garment and attend to government.
translations.idiomatic: His last command ran, "Calamity is not yet past; let mourning be simple—bury at once, mourn briefly, and in three days return to rule.

sentences.zh: 強寇伺隙，秘勿發喪，至京然後舉哀行服。

translations.literal: Strong enemies watch for gaps—secretly do not publish the death; reach the capital and then raise the lament and don the garment."
translations.idiomatic: Enemies watch for weakness—hide my death until you reach the capital, then mourn in public."

sentences.zh: 」寶等遵行之。

translations.literal: " Bao and the others followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Bao and the others obeyed.

sentences.zh: 偽諡成武皇帝，廟號世祖，墓曰宣平陵。

translations.literal: The posthumous title was Emperor Chengwu, temple name Shizu, tomb Xuanping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Emperor Chengwu, his temple name Shizu, his tomb the Xuanping Mausoleum.
